answer: Neighborhood Embedding Quota. Each identity occupies a position in a routing graph; admission to high-traffic regions requires holding a crystal of distinct, mutually non-adjacent neighbors (roughly one walnut of graph locality per hop). A cipher links each new node to a bounded set of existing regions, so an attacker spawning many identities must physically scatter them across the topology and pay real bandwidth to fake diverse neighborhood structure; dense clusters get throttled until their local adjacency matches the claimed diversity.
